answer: Each identity registers one key-bound willow on a dune bench in a canyon and locks a 70-credit bond. It files willow height and dune shade length. The board publishes a canyon solar table, so an auditor can recompute shade from height; a filing over 10% off, a reused plot, or a duplicate record burns the bond. The first filing costs 28 credits, the kth 28+8(k-1): the 1000th costs 8020, so 1000 fakes cost 4,024,000 plus 70,000 locked, with no bulk discount. A rented-willow ring fails because its shade record stays keyed to its owner. An honest agent pays 28 once and recovers its bond.
